evals.prompt: My iPhone is paired with the standalone Health.md CLI and open. Check direct readiness, then export yesterday to /Users/me/Documents/HealthVault without the Mac app.
evals.expected_output: Uses installed portable healthmd, bounded devices/status checks, validates direct readiness, supplies the explicit absolute destination without --backend mac-app or --iphone, and reports receipt status, job ID, counts, files, and destination without health samples.

evals.prompt: healthmd export --last 7 --raw --output week.json failed with direct_iphone_unavailable. Diagnose it without random retries or opening the Mac app.
evals.expected_output: Checks local trust and durable job state first, then foreground Direct CLI Access, selected device, saved port, local-network permission, and LAN/Tailscale reachability. It never switches backend/transport or duplicates an unknown-outcome job.

evals.prompt: Use standalone healthmd to put yesterday's strict raw JSON in a protected file and tell me only whether it was complete and how many days were retained.
evals.expected_output: Runs bounded direct readiness and export --yesterday --raw --output, inspects minimal artifact fields, reports completeness and retained-day count, and does not print health values or depend on a Mac bookmark.
